title: Chapter 1121
paragraphs: Chapter 1121
Episode 258. The Predator of All Dimensions (11)
Kelliark's eyes widened.
My darkest child.
There was only one being that the ego of the Sun God would describe in such a way.
'Helluram...!?'
During his conquest of hundreds of dimensions, Kelliark had never once directly clashed with Helluram's true form. He had only experienced a few battles with her clones.
It wasn't because confronting Helluram was a burden for Kelliark. It was simply because she always fled. Into the abyss, where even the Demon Army found it difficult to track her.

Therefore, whenever Kelliark conquered or destroyed a dimension, he would simply erase her and the abyss itself from existence using that world's Origin Stone. There was no need to endure the trouble of forcibly entering the abyss when he could just erase her from history.

For this reason, Kelliark did not rate Helluram very highly. He acknowledged that she was a transcendent being beyond the Sun God's egos, but she was just one of many special immortals, one who could not dare to oppose him.
Hwiiii..., hwiii...
Suddenly, the sound of a desolate wind began to be heard, and as if a sun eclipse had occurred, the Annihilation Flame Orb was being covered by an darkness of the same size.
'This power... it's not a clone.'
The terrible heat that had spread across the battlefield was rapidly subsiding. The Annihilation Flame Orb, which no one had dared to block, began to cool down as soon as Helluram appeared.
It was the first time he was facing the power of her true form.
However, Kelliark was not particularly surprised to see the Annihilation Flame Orb being covered by darkness, to see that tremendous authority.

'It's on a different level compared to the clones I've encountered before... but according to the Origin Stone's calculations, it's entirely possible. It doesn't deviate much from the expected level. What will you do, Helluram? Can you too show me something that surpasses the Origin Stone's calculations?'
The darkness completely covered the Annihilation Flame Orb.
Finally, from within, Helluram was revealing herself.
'That's... the Witch Helluram.'
Jin and the Genesis Knights, and everyone standing on the battlefield, looked up at the blackened sun.

The form Helluram took seemed no different from a human's. Her face was hidden by a veil, but it was clear even from a distance that it was white, and the black dress that clung to her body trailed so long it seemed to reach the ground.
Except for her clothes, her appearance was not particularly special, but everyone knew from the first moment they saw her that she was the Witch Helluram.
Just as those who have seen darkness immediately know what it means to be dark without anyone teaching them, just as one immediately knows that fire is hot upon facing it.
Normally.
Those who had not reached the rank of a Genesis Knight could fall into the mire of the abyss just by looking at Helluram. If she did not permit them to see her, that is.
The determination Focal had shown in that moment with her words, "I have come to welcome," meant that she would protect people from that.

Therefore, as soon as Helluram appeared, the one who suffered the most was Focal. Focal's sun energy was being crushed by the power of the abyss and was causing unstable waves, but Helluram didn't even pay her any mind.
[Foolish orphan, if you simply needed salvation, there would have been many easier and better paths than this.]
Kelliark let out a chuckle at that desolate voice.
"Salvation? In your eyes, do I look like a being who needs such a thing?"
[Everyone will see you that way. Those who have fallen into the swamp of desire and longing are bound to have the same empty look in their eyes. Whether they stand high or crawl on the ground.]

"To think you dare to judge me, you who were erased from history after running away every time. Well, I'm not curious about your thoughts. But if you wish to make your point, show me the power and authority to back it up. I'm telling you to make me despair."
The Annihilation Flame Orb was covered, but the rivers of magic he had raised were still fiercely twisting and intertwining.

He let out a roar as if nothing had changed even with Helluram's appearance. Then, the darkness and chaotic energy/aura of chaos spread by the witch also thickened, and the energies of the two began to confront each other in earnest.

Their power did not exist only in the limited area of the battlefield but also in all sorts of subspaces extending like deserted islands on the sea, and in the crevices of dimensional entrances leading to other worlds, places that could not normally be perceived.

In all those spaces, the abyss and magic were clashing. Even though the least amount of their power was clashing on the battlefield, the entire area shook as if someone was holding it with both hands a
nd shaking it from the outside.
It wasn't just an earthquake.
The space itself was churning like a sea rolling in a storm. The ground tilted diagonally, and the soldiers instinctively grabbed the ground and looked down at the vast expanse below.
They had been enduring a battle that already seemed unreal, but now the battlefield was churning like a midnight nightmare.
The ground soared up and tilted at a right angle, and the fleet crashed into that earth and fell. The ground was even shattered by the shields.

Then it sank again, churned, and rotated. Physically impossible things happened every second. In those bizarre movements, the space that was momentarily emptied, that is, the underground or the sky, was being replaced by a white, foam-like substance whenever that happened.
No one knew what was inside. But everyone on the battlefield had a gut feeling. That if they fell into that white foam even once, they would never be able to return.
"W-what in the world is this?"
"Ugh, aaaaaargh!"
"Please save me, Lord Rondo!"
Until now, in the Demon Army, even when abandoned as arrow fodder, no matter how fierce the Coalition's attacks were, even when killed on a whim by Kelliark, no one had begged for their life.
They had just charged blindly, like the demons brainwashed by Zito. But now, for the first time, the members of the Demon Army were acting like 'living' people.
Thinking that this was wrong, raising their voices for survival, looking back on what value this war had, and showing on their faces that they did not want to die a dog's death.
That was proof that they were doubting.

The suspicion that Kelliark might face defeat was creating a crack in the loyalty forged by fear and blindness. Kelliark's defeat meant that the Origin Stone would not be able to bring back the dead. The Demon Army would ultimately fail to control time.

Of course, it wasn't just such suspicions that suddenly changed the Demon Army's mages. Helluram, the darkness spreading from her, was staining their inner selves. To overcome that darkness, there were essential elements needed.
A great cause, and bonds.
The desire to conquer matter and time could never be a great cause, and those who were united solely by desire could not realize true bonds.

That was why the Demon Army could not clear away the witch's abyss. Those who had not trembled even after seeing tens, hundreds of thousands being crushed like bugs, were now feeling a fear as if they had been abandoned alone in a cave.
"The enemies are wavering! Knights, protect our allies!"
On the other hand, the Vamel Alliance was no different from before.

No one on the battlefield from the Coalition was there to die. The foundation of a determination to fight for the world even if one eventually dies is different from a mindset of not caring at all about dying. The difference between those with pride and conviction and those without was finally becoming prominent.
[The Indestructible One and I will create a curtain to step on instead of the ground. No matter how the space twists, just find the curtain we made and throw your bodies onto it!]

The response itself was the same for both the Coalition and the Demon Army. Using powers like shadow energy, magic, or sun energy to create an area to support their bodies instead of the distorted space.

What was different was their attitude. No matter how intensely the survival instinct stabbed at their inner selves, the Coalition members reached out more desperately towards those fighting alongside them than for themselves.
"You can't fall!"
"The leader of the Demon Army will eventually waver like them! If we endure, we can go back. Laprarosa is still standing!"
Just as Runtia said, while the entire battlefield churned and distorted, Laprarosa stood tall like a great mountain.
They had to release the curse and let Jin obtain Solderet's legacy.
Even now that the witch had appeared, the Coalition's top priority had not changed. On the contrary, it should be said that it had become more important.

The transcendent beings helping the Coalition on the battlefield now all had different goals from the Coalition. Malugia wanted the ultimate end, and Helluram wanted a world where light did not exist.

Even if Kelliark was defeated and retreated right now, it was a defeat if they couldn't deal with all of them as well. Only the Coalition was struggling not to lose this world. They were fighting to protect memories, recollections, the land, and the people.
"Lo- Lord Kelliark! H-how about retreating? The damage is too, kuaaaargh!"

"You were all laughing so much when you encountered Helluram through the words shown by the Origin Stone, and now you want to run away because you're scared? If I annihilate the enemies, I'll be able to laugh and reminisce about today for a very long time."

Kelliark was bursting into laughter as if he was genuinely enjoying the sight of the Demon Army collapsing. His eyes were bloodshot as if they would burst, and a blood-mixed cough and ragged breaths flowed from his mouth.
He had already shown signs of finally being cornered even before Helluram appeared. Now he clearly looked tired, beyond that, as if he could collapse at any moment and never get up again.
"Heuhh...! Did you think it was something only permitted to you? Not to fall when you should fall. Not to die when you ought to die? Not a chance. I am the true immortal."
Puk...!
Krantel struck down on Kelliark's head. This time too, the blade stopped after splitting his head halfway, and for a moment, he showed a look as if he were a dead person, his eyes losing focus.
It was literally for a fleeting moment. Kelliark pulled out the axe-sword embedded in his head with his left hand and threw Luna away.
'It was only for a moment, but he definitely lost consciousness! His regeneration has slowed down too.'
If they continued to inflict such critical hits, it seemed possible to cut him down before the Origin Stone arrived.
Luna thought so and gripped Krantel again. And Helluram was looking down at Kelliark and speaking thus.
[Kelliark Zipple..., the item you are waiting for, is it really in a whole state? For what reason do you think I have come to find you only now?]
